review_cost.rationale: Approve-adjacent structure, but there is a concrete round of changes I'd require before merging: fix the promise-cache poisoning, replace the effect anti-pattern, clean up the scroll hack, and add at least a few unit tests for the pure logic — all bounded, none structural.

findings.issue: Rejected promises are cached permanently, so a transient network failure makes every later request for that URL fail with the same stale rejection until a full page reload.
findings.suggestion: Evict the cache entry on rejection (request.catch(() => this.cache.delete(url))), or distinguish 404s from transient errors, or move reads to httpResource which handles this correctly.

findings.issue: effect() copies resource value into a separate view signal to avoid the loading flicker — the state-propagation-in-effects anti-pattern the official guidance warns against, and inconsistent with every other page that uses resource.value() directly.
findings.suggestion: Use the v22-documented pattern: linkedSignal over resource.snapshot() to retain the previous value while loading, or at minimum explain the workaround in a comment.

findings.issue: The app ships zero unit tests (skipTests set in angular.json schematics) despite nontrivial pure logic in move-table sorting, filter matching and evolution recursion.
findings.suggestion: Add spec files for MoveTable sorting/aria-sort behavior, the helpers, and PokedexData filtering; the acceptance tests alone won't protect refactors.

findings.issue: Hash-anchor scroll implemented as a plain effect reading window.location.hash with a setTimeout that is never cleaned up, doing manual DOM manipulation.
findings.suggestion: Use afterRenderEffect (the documented tool for post-render DOM work) with onCleanup for the timer, or a router scroll event; remove the redundant moveTables.hasValue() dependency-tracking read.

findings.issue: Loader fans out one HTTP request per move via Promise.all without honoring the loader's abortSignal, so navigating away mid-load leaves dozens of in-flight requests running.
findings.suggestion: Thread the abortSignal through PokeApi (e.g. takeUntil(fromSignal(signal)) on the observable) so stale loads are cancelled, as the resource docs recommend.

findings.issue: Type badges are labeled with humanize(apiName) instead of the English type name the spec asks for; only correct because all 18 type names coincide with their humanized form.
findings.suggestion: Resolve English names from the cached type records (already available via getAllTypes) the way home-page.ts:170 does for cards.

findings.issue: Template calls data.value() about ten times instead of binding once, unlike pokemon-page.ts:71 which uses @let.
findings.suggestion: Use @let view = data.value(); for consistency and cheaper change detection.

findings.issue: Each sortable column has duplicated click handlers on both the th and the nested button with stopPropagation juggling.
findings.suggestion: Keep a single handler on the button and make it fill the th (width/height 100%) for styling.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is listed as a dependency but never imported anywhere in src.
Once view() is non-null the data.error() branch is unreachable, so a failed refetch (API down, bad generation param after a good load) keeps rendering the stale list with no indication of failure.
findings.suggestion: Include error status in the retained snapshot so a failed reload can surface a message or the not-found view.

summary: A genuinely modern Angular 22 codebase: signal inputs, resource()-based loading, URL-driven state, current DI and naming conventions, and clean layering that a reviewer can navigate in minutes. The main merge blockers are a promise cache that permanently poisons failed requests, an effect-to-signal workaround where v22 now documents a proper linkedSignal/snapshot pattern, and the total absence of app-owned unit tests. All required changes are localized — I'd merge after one focused round of fixes.
